'''''Phlox maculata''''', [[common name|commonly]] called '''meadow phlox''',<ref>James H. Locklear. ''Phlox: A Natural History and Gardener's Guide.'' Timber Press, 2011. [https://books.google.com/books?id=L9KgyxXBmCQC&pg=PA169 p. 169.] {{ISBN|9780881929348}}</ref> as well as '''wild sweet William'''<ref name=PLANTS>{{PLANTS |id=PHMA4 |taxon=Phlox maculata |access-date=13 November 2017}}</ref> and '''marsh phlox''',<ref>Alan Branhagen. ''Native Plants of the Midwest: A Comprehensive Guide to the Best 500 Species for the Garden.'' Timber Press, 2016. [https://books.google.com/books?id=ZAZDDQAAQBAJ&pg=PA359 p. 359.] {{ISBN|9781604697773}}</ref>{{efn|"[[Marsh phlox]]" also refers to ''[[Phlox glaberrima|P. glaberrima]]'' and ''[[Phlox kelseyi|P. kelseyi]]''.}} is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Polemoniaceae]], [[native plant|native]] the eastern United States and introduced to eastern Canada.<ref name=PLANTS/> It is a [[perennial]].<ref>{{NPIN|PHMA4|Phlox maculata}}</ref>

Growing to {{convert|2-3|ft|cm|abbr=on}}, this erect, clump-forming [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] produces clusters of fragrant, deep pink flowers in summer. The stiff stems are spotted red, hence the Latin [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''maculata''. It prefers damp, well-drained soil in full sun. It is less prone to [[powdery mildew]] than the related ''[[Phlox paniculata]]''.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=e590
| title = ''Phlox maculata'' | publisher = Missouri Botanical Garden | access-date = 8 February 2021}}</ref>

The following [[cultivar]]s have received the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]:
* 'Alpha'<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/97818/Phlox-maculata-Alpha/Details | title = ''Phlox maculata'' 'Alpha' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 18 January 2021}}</ref> (lilac)
* 'Natascha'<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/105104/Phlox-maculata-Natascha/Details | title = ''Phlox maculata'' 'Natascha' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 18 January 2021}}</ref> (pink and white)
* 'Omega'<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/100095/Phlox-maculata-Omega/Details | title = ''Phlox maculata'' 'Omega' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 18 January 2021}}</ref> (white with a red eye)
